questions.q: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.
questions.s:
Answer:better

Explanation:
The sentence is making a comparison between two points in time — when they left for Mexico and now.
When comparing two things, we use the comparative form of adjectives.

  • The word "good" becomes "better" in the comparative form.

  • Saying "in good condition than..." is incorrect — it should be "in better condition than..."

Let’s review the options:

  • better → ✅ Correct comparative form of "good"

  • excellent → ❌ Not a comparative; also not used with "than"

  • more good → ❌ Incorrect (never use "more" with "good"; use "better")

  • best → ❌ Superlative form, used when comparing more than two

Correct sentence:
When they left for Mexico, their house was in better condition than it is now.

o: by far the brightest
by so far the brighter
so far most bright
questions.s:
Explanation:

Error Analysis:

  • "So far the bright" is grammatically incorrect.

  • We are comparing one student with the rest of the class, which means a superlative is required (like brightest, not "bright").

  • Also, the correct idiomatic phrase is "by far the brightest", used to emphasize a superlative.

✅ Correct Usage:

You are by far the brightest student in the class.

📘 Explanation:

  • "by far": an intensifier used with a superlative (e.g., the best, the smartest, the brightest).

  • "brightest": superlative of "bright", correct in this comparison context.

❌ Option-wise Analysis:

  • A. by far the brightest ✅
     ✔ Correct structure: intensifier + superlative.

  • B. No improvement ❌
     ✖ "so far the bright" is ungrammatical.

  • C. by so far the brighter ❌
     ✖ Incorrect word order, and "brighter" is a comparative, not superlative.

  • D. so far most bright ❌
     ✖ "most bright" is awkward and unidiomatic; also "so far" doesn’t collocate well here.

✅ Final Answer: A. by far the brightest (अबतककासबसेहोशियारछात्र)

questions.q: The school organized a science fairs for the students.
questions.s:
The correct option is (b) "a science fairs." The error in the sentence lies in the incorrect pluralization of "science fair." The correct form should be "science fairs" to match the singular "a."

In the sentence "The school organized a science fair for the students," the word "science" functions as an adjective modifying the noun "fair."

When a noun like "science" is used to modify another noun (in this case, "fair"), it functions as an adjective, providing additional information about the type or nature of the noun it modifies.

the corrected sentence should be: "The school organized a science fair for the students."
